# Madeira Tour

> Fully arranged Madeira trips for 1 to 36 guests: pool apartments in Funchal, airport pickup in two 18-seat minibuses, a 14-guest yacht, local guides and ready-made routes to the island’s finest places.

Madeira Tour is a travel organiser based in Funchal, Madeira (Portugal). We arrange complete holidays on Madeira for travellers from Europe, from a single guest to groups of 36. The site is available in Ukrainian, English, German, Polish, French and Russian.

## What we offer
- Apartments with a swimming pool in Funchal, with balconies over Funchal bay — 1 to 36 guests.
- Airport meet-and-greet at Madeira Airport (FNC) with two 18-seat minibuses (36 seats), also used for every excursion.
- A yacht for up to 14 guests: dolphin watching, swimming coves, Cabo Girão from the sea, sunset sailings. Larger groups sail in turns.
- Local guides to Madeira’s finest places, tailored to each group’s wishes, age and fitness.
- Corporate events and celebrations in central Funchal, next to the Plaza Madeira shopping centre.
- Trail registration for walking routes (PR trails charge non-residents and need booked start times).

## Itineraries
### Madeira Classic (5 days · 4 nights)
Peaks at sunrise, before the clouds rise. The west as a clockwise loop: lava pools in the warmest hours, Fanal when the fog rolls in, sunset at the westernmost cape.
- Day 1, Arrival & Old Town: Madeira Airport (FNC) (Met at the arrivals exit); Pool apartments (Check-in, time by the pool); Rua de Santa Maria (Dinner in the Old Town)
- Day 2, East: above the clouds: Pico do Arieiro (Sunrise above a sea of clouds); Balcões (Levada stroll to the ‘balcony’); Santana (Palheiro cottages, lunch up north); Ponta de São Lourenço (PR8 path to the island’s edge); Machico (Machico beach, back to Funchal)
- Day 3, West & north: Câmara de Lobos (Coffee above the fishing harbour); Cabo Girão (Glass skywalk, 580 m up); Véu da Noiva (The Bride’s Veil waterfall); Seixal (Black-sand beach); Porto Moniz (Lunch and a swim in the lava pools); Ribeira da Janela (The sea stack with a ‘window’); Fanal Forest (The misty til forest); Ponta do Pargo (Sunset at the lighthouse)
- Day 4, Funchal & the ocean: Mercado dos Lavradores market (Market and fruit tasting); Monte Palace Garden (Cable car, Monte Palace garden, toboggan ride); Cabo Girão from the sea (Yacht: dolphins, Cabo Girão from the sea, a swim); Central Funchal · Plaza Madeira (Farewell dinner in the centre)
- Day 5, Departure: Pool apartments (Breakfast and a last swim); Madeira Airport (FNC) (Transfer to the airport)

### Peaks & Levadas (6 days · 5 nights)
Linear trails with no backtracking: we drop you at the start and collect you at the finish. The hardest crossing comes on day two while legs are fresh, and the sea at the end to rest them.
- Day 1, Arrival: Madeira Airport (FNC) (Met at the airport); Pool apartments (Check-in and a trail briefing); Rua de Santa Maria (Dinner in the Old Town)
- Day 2, Roof of the island: Pico do Arieiro (Sunrise and the start of the PR1); Pico Ruivo (The 1,862 m summit); Achada do Teixeira (Finish: the minibus is waiting); Santana (Late lunch in Santana)
- Day 3, The Green Cauldron levada: Queimadas (Start at the Queimadas houses); Caldeirão Verde (Tunnels and the Caldeirão Verde falls); Balcões (On the way back: Balcões lookout)
- Day 4, Plateau & misty forest: Rabaçal · 25 Fontes (The 25 Fontes and Risco levadas); Fanal Forest (Fanal in the fog); Ponta do Pargo (Sunset at the lighthouse)
- Day 5, Cape & sea: Ponta de São Lourenço (PR8 in the morning, before the heat); Machico (Lunch in Machico); Cabo Girão from the sea (Sunset cruise on the yacht)
- Day 6, Departure: Mercado dos Lavradores market (Market and souvenirs); Madeira Airport (FNC) (Transfer to the airport)

### Island & Ocean (5 days · 4 nights)
Little driving and plenty of water: sea, pools, gardens. The one long drive goes north, with a swim in the middle of the day. Add a day on Porto Santo if you like.
- Day 1, Arrival & seafront: Madeira Airport (FNC) (Met at the airport); Pool apartments (Check-in, pool); Funchal Marina (Seafront walk at sunset)
- Day 2, A day at sea: Funchal Marina (Setting sail); Cabo Girão from the sea (Cabo Girão from the sea, dolphin watching); Garajau cove (A swim in Garajau cove); Pool apartments (Pool and dinner)
- Day 3, Funchal & gardens: Mercado dos Lavradores market (Farmers’ market); Monte Palace Garden (Cable car, garden, toboggan); Madeira Botanical Garden (Cable car down to the Botanical Garden); Câmara de Lobos (Poncha and sunset over Churchill’s bay)
- Day 4, Lava pools: Véu da Noiva (Waterfall over the ocean); Seixal (Black-sand beach); Porto Moniz (Swimming in the natural pools); Fanal Forest (A short forest walk)
- Day 5, Departure: Pool apartments (A morning by the pool); Madeira Airport (FNC) (Transfer to the airport)

### Team Weekend (4 days · 3 nights)
Two minibuses move the whole group together. While part of the team is on the yacht, the rest explore Monte, so nobody waits. The party comes on the last night, once everyone has shared the island.
- Day 1, Team arrival: Madeira Airport (FNC) (Two minibuses collect the whole group); Pool apartments (Check-in, drinks by the pool); Rua de Santa Maria (Welcome dinner in the Old Town)
- Day 2, Above the clouds: Pico do Arieiro (Sunrise together on the summit); Santana (Santana and lunch); Ponta de São Lourenço (Team walk on the PR8); Machico (Back via Machico)
- Day 3, Sea & celebration: Cabo Girão from the sea (Yacht in 2–3 sailings of 14); Monte Palace Garden (Meanwhile: Monte garden and toboggan); Central Funchal · Plaza Madeira (Party in central Funchal by Plaza Madeira)
- Day 4, Departure: Mercado dos Lavradores market (Market and souvenirs); Madeira Airport (FNC) (Transfer for the whole group)

## 21 places on Madeira we visit
- **Pico do Arieiro** (Central massif · 1,818 m; 32.7357, -16.9289): The road climbs almost to the summit, so a sunrise above a sea of clouds takes no hard ascent. This is also where the PR1 begins: a ridge path of tunnels and stone steps to Pico Ruivo. Madeira’s third-highest peak. Clouds usually rise by mid-morning, which is why we arrive before dawn.
- **Pico Ruivo** (Highest point · 1,862 m; 32.759, -16.9427): The roof of Madeira. Reach it in about an hour from Achada do Teixeira, or by the full PR1 crossing from Arieiro. On a clear day both coasts are in view at once. We drop the group at one trailhead and collect it at the other, so nobody walks back the same way.
- **Ponta de São Lourenço** (Eastern cape · Caniçal; 32.7442, -16.7076): The island’s eastern tip looks nothing like the rest of Madeira: bare volcanic ridges in red, ochre and black, with wind and ocean on both sides. The PR8 path leads to a lookout hill above the very end of the cape. Come late in the afternoon, when the low sun turns the cliffs copper-red.
- **Santana** (North coast; 32.8086, -16.8812): Triangular cottages with thatched roofs, the palheiros, were once ordinary farmhouses on the north coast. Today they are the emblem of Madeira, and the hills around them are still farmed the old way, terrace by terrace. The whole municipality of Santana has been a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 2011.
- **Caldeirão Verde** (Levada PR9 · Queimadas; 32.775, -16.915): The path follows a levada through ancient laurel forest, ducks through several tunnels and ends beneath a tall waterfall pouring into a green rock basin. Hence the name: the Green Cauldron. Madeira is crossed by more than 2,000 km of levadas, irrigation channels cut by hand since the 15th century.
- **Balcões** (Ribeiro Frio · viewpoint; 32.739, -16.884): A flat 1.5 km stroll along a levada brings you to a ‘balcony’ over a deep valley, facing the island’s highest peaks. One of Madeira’s easiest walks with one of its best views. The local chaffinches are so used to visitors that they land on your palm.
- **Curral das Freiras** (Nuns’ Valley · Eira do Serrado; 32.7116, -16.9611): A village at the bottom of a vast mountain bowl, walled in by peaks on every side. From the Eira do Serrado lookout it looks like a model. Come in autumn, for the chestnut festival. In 1566 the nuns of the Santa Clara convent fled here from French pirates, which gave the valley its name: the Nuns’ Refuge.
- **Rua de Santa Maria** (Funchal Old Town; 32.6478, -16.9031): Funchal’s oldest street has become an open-air gallery: nearly every door is painted by a different artist. By day it is cafés and craft shops; by night, grilled fish and tables on the cobbles. The ‘Art of Open Doors’ project began in 2010 to bring a neglected quarter back to life.
- **Monte Palace Garden** (Monte · above Funchal; 32.675, -16.9025): A tropical garden on the hillside above the city: Japanese pagodas, koi ponds, tree ferns and hundreds of azulejo panels. You ride up by cable car from the seafront and come down in a wicker toboggan. The basket toboggans have carried passengers since the 19th century: two drivers in white and straw hats steer them two kilometres downhill.
- **Madeira Botanical Garden** (Funchal · above the bay; 32.6622, -16.8958): Mosaic flower beds of red and lime-green plants step down in terraces towards a view of all Funchal and the ocean. Around them grow palms, cacti, dragon trees and plants found only on Madeira. A cable car flies here straight from Monte. The garden opened in 1960 at Quinta do Bom Sucesso, the estate of the Reid family, founders of the legendary Reid’s hotel.
- **Câmara de Lobos** (Fishing town; 32.648, -16.977): Colourful boats in the bay, houses on a rock above the sea, and bars pouring poncha, the island’s own drink of sugarcane rum, honey and lemon. From here the road runs west to Cabo Girão. Winston Churchill painted this bay in 1950, and the lookout above it bears his name.
- **Cabo Girão** (Glass skywalk · 580 m; 32.656, -17.004): One of Europe’s highest sea cliffs. You stand on a glass floor with 580 metres of air beneath you and tiny farm plots at the water’s edge, which farmers still reach by cable car. Those plots are fajãs: flat land formed by ancient rockfalls.
- **Ponta do Sol** (South-west coast; 32.68, -17.1): A white town squeezed between cliffs and banana terraces, and one of the sunniest on the island; the name means ‘Sun Point’. A seafront, a pier and a sunset that turns the whole cove gold. In 2021 it became one of Europe’s first ‘digital nomad villages’.
- **Porto Moniz** (Natural lava pools; 32.868, -17.17): Cooled lava formed rock pools at the shoreline, refilled by the Atlantic swell. You can swim here even when the ocean is rough: the waves break on the rocks while the water inside stays calm. It is real seawater with no chlorine, refreshed by the tide and every big wave.
- **Seixal** (Black-sand beach · north; 32.824, -17.111): A village on a green headland under sheer mountains, with a beach of black volcanic sand beside it. Perhaps the most photogenic spot on the north coast: dark sand, turquoise water, waterfalls on the slopes. The black sand is crushed basalt, and on a sunny day it gets much hotter than pale sand.
- **Véu da Noiva** (Waterfall · Seixal to São Vicente; 32.82, -17.095): A slender waterfall leaps off a sheer cliff straight into the ocean. The best angle is from the lookout on the old coastal road, with the whole north shore stretching towards Porto Moniz. The name means ‘bride’s veil’, and in a breeze the water really does scatter into a white haze.
- **Fanal Forest** (Paul da Serra plateau; 32.81, -17.145): Centuries-old til trees with twisted limbs on a green meadow, often wrapped in fog. Then the forest looks like a set for a fairy tale, and photographers come here precisely for the mist. Fanal is part of the Laurisilva, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999 and the largest surviving laurel forest on Earth.
- **Ribeira da Janela** (Sea stacks · north-west; 32.864, -17.152): Basalt sea stacks rise from a restless ocean beside a beach of black pebbles. The light is best at sunset, and you can hear the stones rolling in the surf from far away. Janela means ‘window’: the waves bored a hole right through one of the islets, and it named the whole valley.
- **Ponta do Pargo** (Lighthouse · westernmost point; 32.814, -17.264): A lighthouse at the edge of a high cliff on the island’s far west. The best place to watch the sun drop into the Atlantic, with nothing but ocean between you and the Americas. The light has shone since 1922; the cape is named after a huge pargo, a sea bream, caught here by the first Portuguese sailors.
- **Desertas Islands** (Nature reserve · by yacht; 32.52, -16.51): Three uninhabited islands on the south-east horizon, visible from Funchal. By yacht it is a day of open ocean: dolphins, seabirds and clear coves beneath red cliffs. They shelter one of the last colonies of the Mediterranean monk seal, and a giant wolf spider found in a single valley of Deserta Grande and nowhere else.
- **Porto Santo** (Sister island · 9 km of beach; 33.05, -16.34): The sister island has what Madeira lacks: nine kilometres of golden sand and calm, warm water. The ferry from Funchal takes about two and a half hours; come for a day or stay the night. Christopher Columbus lived here after marrying the daughter of the island’s first governor; his house in Vila Baleira is now a museum.

## FAQ
**How do I get to Madeira from Europe?** Direct flights to Madeira’s Cristiano Ronaldo International Airport (FNC) leave from many European cities: about 1 h 45 min from Lisbon and 3.5 to 5 hours from most capitals. We meet you at the arrivals exit, and Funchal is about 20 minutes away.

**How many people can you host?** From one traveller to a group of 36. Two 18-seat minibuses move the whole group together, and the yacht takes up to 14 guests per sailing, so larger groups sail in turns.

**What does a fully arranged trip include?** Airport pickup and transfers, pool apartments, guided excursions in our own vehicles, a yacht outing, restaurant bookings and, if you wish, a corporate event or party in central Funchal. You choose what goes into the package.

**Can I change the itinerary?** Yes. The ready-made routes are a starting point: we change the order of days, the pace and the places to suit your wishes, ages and fitness. Each day is confirmed the evening before against the forecast, because mountain weather turns fast.

**When is the best time to visit Madeira?** All year. Winter days are usually 18 to 20 °C and summer days 24 to 27 °C, and the sea warms to 22 to 24 °C in August and September. Funchal holds its Flower Festival in spring and its Wine Festival in late summer, and its 2006 New Year fireworks entered the Guinness World Records.

**Do I need permits for the mountain trails?** Most official walking routes (PR) charge non-residents a fee, and the popular ones need a start time booked in advance. We register your group ahead, so nobody waits or queues on the day.

**Do I need a rental car?** No. We drive you to every excursion in our own minibuses with a driver, and we plan linear trails so the vehicle waits at the finish.

**Is it suitable for children and older travellers?** Yes. Every route has easy options: roadside viewpoints, flat levadas, natural pools and cable cars. We set the pace for whoever needs the most time.

**Can you organise a corporate event?** Yes, in the very centre of Funchal next to Plaza Madeira. We handle the evening’s format, transfers for the whole group and a programme for the other days: the yacht, the mountains, the Monte gardens.

**How do I book?** Fill in the booking form with your dates, group size, itinerary and wishes. We reply with a detailed proposal and price, and once you confirm, we book the accommodation, transport and guides.
